subject: Discovery: observability & eval gating for iCore integration
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@icore.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: observability & eval gating for iCore integration

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I misstated anything, please correct me inline.

Key pain points you described:
- Limited visibility into model regressions post-deploy (we heard gaps in catching behavioral regressions before they reach prod).
- Siloed telemetry: token-level latency and KV/cache hits are not surfaced in your dashboards today.
- Cost spikes during batch inference runs and unclear per-route unit economics.
- Lack of a stable evaluation baseline (you don’t have a canonical prompt set + automated regression alerts tied to releases).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Inference: GKE-hosted custom service that calls open models (Llama-3 family) via an internal gateway.
- Observability: Datadog for service metrics, Papertrail for logs; no token-level tracing yet.
- Release process: weekly model rollouts, manual smoke checks.

Success criteria you called out:
- Regression detection before >90% of customer-facing releases.
- P99 latency for short conversational queries <= 250ms (regional SLA target).
- Reduce per-1k-token cost on peak routes by ~20% through batching/caching/quantization guidance.

What Redwood can deliver in the initial eval/sandbox:
- A 2-week sandbox that wires our tracing hooks into your GKE service (token-level latency, KV cache hits/misses).
- A sample dashboard (attached) showing model-version comparisons, regression deltas, and cost breakdown by route.
- An eval checklist (attached) to capture canonical prompts, evaluation metrics, and guardrail thresholds.
- A regression alert playbook that can trigger CI gating or rollback policies.

Attachments: icore-eval-checklist.xlsx (checklist for canonical prompts + metrics), dashboard-mock.png (sample dashboard), slo-matrix.csv (proposed SLOs).

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm stakeholders for the sandbox (who can provide AWS/GCP service account & Datadog read access).
2) Confirm canonical prompt owners and a short list (~30 prompts) we can use for the first run.
3) Are there any audit/SOC requirements we should account for in the sandbox (I saw you mentioned SOC‑2 earlier)?
4) Proposed kickoff: Mon 2026-09-20 10:00 AM PT. Does that work?

I'll schedule the kickoff tentatively and share access details once I get confirmation on stakeholders.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@icore.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 17:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: observability & eval gating for iCore integration

Thanks, Stephanie — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Stack correction: we run on GCP (GKE) and call models through a lightweight gateway, yes. Datadog is our primary SRE tool.
2) Audit: we do need SOC 2 Type II evidence for any production-facing integration; for the sandbox we can provide a limited user that doesn't require elevated PII access.
3) Canonical prompts: happy to own the prompt set. We'll compile ~40 prompts and share them by EOD Thursday.
4) Tracing hooks: can you describe at a high level what data Redwood collects? Specifically: token-level timestamps, model-version id, route name, and KV cache hits would be ideal. Anything that includes raw payloads will be a non-starter for now.

I've attached a short internal SLO doc (icore-internal-slo.pdf) that lists our baseline latency & availability targets. See attached for reference.

If you can confirm the data collection list and that the sandbox won’t ingest PII, we can proceed with the Monday kickoff.

—
Jordan Ellis
Director, Platforms | iCore Analytics
j.ellis@icore.ai | +1 (206) 555-0890

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@icore.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: observability & eval gating for iCore integration

Appreciate the clarifications, Jordan — and thanks for the SLO doc. High-level answers below; I’ll bring the instrumenting checklist to the kickoff.

What Redwood collects in the sandbox (non-PII defaults):
- Token-level latency stamps (no raw user text by default; we can hash or truncate inputs per your requirements).
- Model version identifier and inference config (quantization profile, sequence length).
- Route name / endpoint, per-request cost estimate and token counts.
- KV cache diagnostics: hit/miss counts and approximate cache occupancy.
- Aggregates for dashboards and per-release eval diffs (we do not store raw prompts unless you opt into storing the canonical set for reproducible evals).

Guardrails we enforce for the eval run:
- Default redact/hash of payloads; customers must opt-in to keep full inputs for debugging.
- Retention policy: sandbox data kept 14 days unless you request longer.
- Alerts: configurable thresholds (regression delta %, p99 latency breach, cache hit drop) with webhook/SNS or PagerDuty integration.

I’ve re-attached the eval checklist and dashboard mock. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-artifacts.

Next steps: once you share the prompt set (Thu EOD), we’ll:
- Import prompts into the eval harness and run a baseline (2 business days).
- Turn on token tracing and send an initial dashboard snapshot.

We’ll keep everything non-PII unless you tell us otherwise. Happy to have a short security sync prior to the kickoff if you prefer.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery: observability & eval gating for iCore integration

Looping in from the engineering side — thanks for the notes, Jordan. A couple items from our side: 

- Marcus here (Solutions Engineering). I’ll own the rollout guardrails and the canary plan during the sandbox.
- For the kickoff: Mon 2026-09-20 10:00 AM PT works for me. I’ll add a short agenda (instrumentation checklist, Datadog integration, evaluation metrics) and invite our SRE/security lead if you want them there.
- Pricing note: the initial 2-week sandbox is complementary. If iCore opts into the private eval (longer retention, storing canonical prompts), we’ll follow up with a scoped estimate — I’ll include rough numbers in the sales playbook after the baseline run.

On the trace payload: Stephanie covered the defaults — from an SRE perspective we typically ask customers to annotate any fields they consider sensitive so we can redact at source. Jordan, do you have a security contact we should loop in?

Looking forward to the kickoff.
